tests.name: Capabilities expose chronological one-to-three events and conditional goal probability rather than a win rate
Two audited physical decks have a declared unknown order and no fabricated prior shuffle
One draw branches over each remaining physical copy with exact one-in-three mass
Analysis never changes its physical source, real unknown deck order or the global laboratory
Already having a goal before the requested number of events does not end the tree early
Three chronological events contain two own draws without replacement and one intervening rival draw
Repeated physical copies keep separate UIDs and sum to the correct joint probability
Explicit-priority PASS windows settle before each draw checkpoint and support the real multi-turn history
The rival controls real attack choices and minimizes the goal rather than being chosen cooperatively
The goal-probability report keeps its explicit information, action-domain and provisional-score assumptions
A one-node budget conserves all omitted physical mass as unknown rather than failure
A chance-branch limit keeps uncovered copies as exact aggregate unknown weight
A depth horizon before the second event retains uncertainty instead of a fabricated probability
An explicit empty-of-applicable-actions policy is reported unknown
Cancellation before analysis does not return a partial tree disguised as accepted evidence
Cancellation after yielding also discards the incomplete analysis
Stale format or catalogue context rejects analysis and imported evidence
A changed live deck cancels analysis even when the source itself was not changed
An unrecorded current-state move is rejected rather than treated as an observed prefix
Passcodes, owner, actor, goal and context changes cannot be smuggled through an imported source
Invalid limits and unsupported goal fields fail closed
Tampering with chance weight, remaining-copy count or physical identity is rejected by fresh replay
A forged success leaf, score, interval, missing branch or requested checkpoint is rejected
Tampering with real conditional action cost, actor or target is rejected
Reducing exported search budgets cannot relabel a larger conditional proof as a one-node analysis
A report is serializable, separately verified and never advertises ordinary causal replay
Cooperative verification returns exactly the synchronous canonical result for a small accepted report
Cooperative verification traverses a real priority tree in increasing eight-node chunks with the same result
Synchronous and cooperative verification reject the same tampered physical mass and conditional action record
An already aborted cooperative verification emits no accepted or partial report and does not change its source
A timer can cancel cooperative verification between chunks while the laboratory stays unchanged
A progress callback can cancel cooperative verification without mutating the imported evidence
Changing the live build during a verification yield rejects stale evidence before returning a canonical report
A changed explicit source snapshot is checked again after asynchronous replay
QA enumeration diagnostic keeps uncertainty for legal manual actions omitted by the registered enumeration
An incomplete handler outside the explicitly declared action-type policy does not corrupt the admitted-domain result
QA controller diagnostic preserves unknown mass when an atomic action contains the other players replacement choice
QA mixed-actor diagnostic does not assign two players free actions to one cooperative controller
QA information-order diagnostic fixes the choice before future draws and computes max-of-expectations, not expectation-of-clairvoyant-max

limitations: The QA commit adapter tests information order and is not a shipped card rule.
All probabilities are conditional hypothetical goal probabilities under the report assumptions and registered action domain.
No full test runner or browser build is executed by this suite.
